Named customers

Organisations named in public sources as using this vendor’s tracked products, strongest evidence first.

No named customer could be confirmed from public sources. Vendors often cannot name bank customers, so this is not a finding about adoption.

How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Reputation

Adverse items are attributed to their sources and need one primary source or two independent ones before they are published.

Reputation
Regulatory actionsMeta disclosed in its 2025 Form 10-K: a EUR 1.2 billion fine from the Irish Data Protection Commission in May 2023 over EU-US data transfers, under appeal and stayed; a fine of about EUR 798 million from the European Commission in November 2024 concerning Facebook Marketplace, under appeal; a EUR 200 million fine under the EU Digital Markets Act in April 2025 over its subscription-for-no-ads model, under appeal; and an FTC administrative proceeding alleging children's-privacy violations and consent-order deficiencies, stayed pending Meta's court challenges. It also disclosed inquiries by the FTC, members of Congress and state attorneys general into AI chatbots. Independently evidenced high confidence US Securities and Exchange Commission (EDGAR) (primary filing, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)
LitigationMeta disclosed in its 2025 Form 10-K: judgment in its favour on 2025-11-18 in the FTC antitrust case, which the FTC appealed in January 2026; a Spanish court's award of about EUR 542 million to publishers in November 2025, under appeal; a California jury verdict in August 2025 in a privacy case concerning the Flo Health app, with damages undetermined; state attorney general actions over youth safety, including a New Mexico trial set for September 2026; and copyright suits in the US, Europe and Canada over the use of copyrighted material to train AI models. Timeline

  1. 2026-10-15 · launch Meta Platforms
    Meta releases open weights for Muse Spark Open under the Muse Model License

    Meta announced on 2026-10-15 the open-weight Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter model with a one-million-token context window, under its Muse Model License. Weights are on Hugging Face, Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden and Microsoft Foundry, with hosted inference from providers including Together AI and Fireworks AI. The model card says offering the model as a paid service needs a separate agreement with Meta above US$20 million of revenue in 12 months. Meta Platforms (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)Meta Platforms (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  2. 2026-08-10 · launch Meta Platforms
    Meta releases Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter open-weight model under Apache 2.0

    BetaNews reported on 2026-08-10 that Meta had released Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter open-weight model distilled from Muse Spark 1.2 under the Apache 2.0 licence, downloadable from Hugging Face, and that Mark Zuckerberg said the weights of Muse Spark 1.2 would also be released. The date shown is the report's date; the report places the release within the preceding day. BetaNews (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)Meta Platforms (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  3. 2026-07-09 · launch Meta Platforms
    Meta opens Muse Spark 1.1 to US developers through a paid Meta Model API preview

    Reuters reported on 2026-07-09 that Meta released developer access to Muse Spark 1.1 in public preview through the Meta Model API for developers in the United States, at US$1.25 per million input tokens and US$4.25 per million output tokens. The report said the original Muse Spark, from the superintelligence team Meta formed in 2025, debuted in April 2026 and was expected to replace the Llama models in Meta's own apps. Reuters (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  4. 2026-05-20 · layoff Meta Platforms
    Meta cuts about 8,000 jobs, roughly 10% of its workforce

    Reported by NPR on 2026-04-23 and Al Jazeera on 2026-05-20: Meta told staff it would cut about 8,000 jobs, roughly 10% of its workforce, with effect from 20 May 2026, and would not fill about 6,000 open roles, as it increased spending on AI. NPR said a Meta spokesperson confirmed an internal memo first published by Bloomberg. Al Jazeera reported that about 7,000 employees were being moved into AI-related roles. NPR (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)Al Jazeera (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  5. 2025-11-19 · litigation Meta Platforms
    Spanish court awards about EUR 542 million against Meta Ireland in publishers' case

    Meta disclosed in its 2025 Form 10-K that on 2025-11-19 a Spanish court, in a case brought by the media association AMI against Meta Ireland, found no abuse of dominance but upheld an unfair-competition claim and awarded damages of about EUR 542 million. Meta said it has appealed. US Securities and Exchange Commission (EDGAR) (primary filing, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  6. 2025-11-18 · litigation Meta Platforms
    Court rules for Meta in FTC antitrust case; FTC appeals in January 2026

    Meta disclosed in its 2025 Form 10-K that on 2025-11-18 the court granted judgment in its favour in the antitrust case the US Federal Trade Commission filed in December 2020 over the Instagram and WhatsApp acquisitions, after a trial from 14 April to 27 May 2025, and that the FTC filed a notice of appeal on 2026-01-20. US Securities and Exchange Commission (EDGAR) (primary filing, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)
